title: What Is Frontend Development?
description: Understand what frontend engineers actually build, how frontend differs from design and backend work, and why HTML, CSS, and JavaScript form the platform foundation.

objectives.statement: Explain in plain language what frontend development encompasses.
Identify the distinct roles of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a client application.

content.title: Welcome to Frontend Engineering
content.hook: Every website or web application you use runs on a client runtime inside your browser. But what does a frontend engineer actually build?
content.context: Frontend engineering connects user experience designs to real browser APIs, data pipelines, and responsive rendering engines.
goals: Differentiate frontend development from visual design and backend databases.
Understand how HTML, CSS, and JavaScript collaborate to form user interfaces.

content.title: Frontend Is More Than Aesthetics
content.text: Frontend development is the practice of building everything users see and interact with in a web browser. This includes document hierarchy, layout algorithms, accessibility trees, client state management, network caching, and interactive input handling.

callout.text: Common misconception: 'Frontend is just making things look pretty.' While aesthetics matter, frontend engineering involves complex state machines, data synchronization, security, and performance optimizations.

content.keyTakeaway: Frontend engineers build reliable, responsive, and accessible client-side software systems.

content.title: The Web Platform Trio
content.description: HTML provides structure and meaning. CSS controls styling and layout. JavaScript drives dynamic behavior and runtime state.

content.title: A Minimal Interactive Button in Three Layers
content.description: Notice how HTML declares the element, CSS styles its state, and JavaScript attaches a click listener.
content.code:
<!-- 1. HTML: Semantic Element -->
<button id="counter-btn" class="primary-btn">Clicks: 0</button>

<!-- 2. CSS: Visual Presentation -->
<style>
  .primary-btn {
    background-color: #2563eb;
    color: white;
    padding: 10px 20px;
    border: none;
    border-radius: 6px;
    cursor: pointer;
  }
</style>

<!-- 3. JavaScript: Runtime Behavior -->
<script>
  let count = 0;
  const btn = document.getElementById('counter-btn');
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    count += 1;
    btn.textContent = `Clicks: ${count}`;
  });
</script>

content.question: Which of the following tasks is primarily the responsibility of a frontend engineer?

options.text: Writing SQL database migrations for user account tables
options.hint: Database tables and migrations are backend persistence concerns.

options.text: Implementing a responsive dropdown menu with keyboard accessibility (WCAG)
options.hint: Think about what runs in the user's browser.

options.text: Configuring load balancers and physical server clusters
options.hint: Infrastructure and DevOps manage server clusters.

options.text: Creating high-fidelity vector illustrations in design software

content.explanation: Frontend engineers implement interactive, accessible, and responsive components in browser environments.

feedback.correct: Correct! Building accessible, responsive interactive UI components is a core frontend responsibility.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Remember that frontend engineers focus on client-side behavior, accessibility, and browser rendering.

content.title: Key Takeaways
takeaways: Frontend development focuses on client-side applications running in user agents (browsers).
HTML declares structure, CSS controls presentation, and JavaScript powers dynamic behavior.
Frontend is an engineering discipline requiring attention to accessibility, responsiveness, and state management.
